title: wslua: Add Lua Debugger
description:
- Introduce a Lua debugger dialog with syntax highlighting, paused-line
  indicator, file tree, and toolbar actions.
- Support variable inspection
- Provide stack-trace visualization that enables navigation for Lua frames
- Allow setting breakpoints both in main scripts and callback contexts;
  breakpoints can be toggled active/inactive, persist across runs and
  auto-loads on startup.
- Automatic UI activation when the first breakpoint hits.
- The debugger can be disabled manually.

**Remaining issues to check**
- [ ] Crash when debugger is paused in a dissector and the user select a different packet which also would hit a break point
- [ ] Code review commits on top of the base
  - [ ] "Debugger UX and settings improvements"
  - [ ] "Debugger security, crash and UX fixes"
  - [ ] "Debugger data races and gutter perf fixes"
  - [ ] "Handle re-entrant seek_read during Lua debugger pause"
  - [ ] "Defer plugin reload when debugger paused to prevent crash"
  - [ ] "Fix Lua debugger step skipping to next packet"
  - [ ] "Allow closing the Lua debugger when paused"
- [x] Crash while debugging the [any_file.lua](/uploads/ce7483f504eaae26a47751daa04ede1f/any_file.lua) script
- [x] Crash while reload Lua plugins when debugger paused
- [x] Issues reading/writing lua_debugger.json at dialog loading
- [x] "Step to next line" on the last line of a dissector script
- [ ] Check if the "Lua console" can be used instead of the new "Evaluate"
- [ ] Hidden columns in the variables tree and file tree

notes.body:
This feature looks very interesting. I have not looked at the implementation (yet), but after trying it for some minutes I have some questions and comments.
* The first thing I wanted to do was to edit the Lua script and Reload. Is this something you have been thinking about doing in this dialog?
* The next thing I wanted to do was "Step to next line". Is this in your plans?
* Some users may complain about only Dark mode in the code view dialog. I think we should have both Light and Dark mode.
* I found some minor/annoying usability issues:
  * Dialog size not remembered
  * Not able to move the column separator between Name and Value (difficult to read long values)
  * Wireshark Preferences dialog always on top making it hard to debug preferences code
  * The "Enabled" checkbox changes text to "Disabled" without being checked. This is inconsistent and hard to understand.
* I made it crash in some cases. I will try to recreate and describe this.

Thank you for your feedback. I really appreciate it.

> The first thing I wanted to do was to edit the Lua script and Reload. Is this something you have been thinking about doing in this dialog?

This is an important use case. I will cover it.

> The next thing I wanted to do was "Step to next line". Is this in your plans?
Step to Next line should be feasible. The is already a run to this line feature, which is available via context menu. Something like a Step into or Step out will be very hard to be implemented since we have no deep understanding of the language. (no AST for example)

> Some users may complain about only Dark mode in the code view dialog. I think we should have both Light and Dark mode.

This should be no problem.

> Dialog size not remembered

This makes sense but I still struggle to deal with the preferences during the startup phase.

> Not able to move the column separator between Name and Value (difficult to read long values)

I am looking for a solution for this. I want that the columns are stretched by default but the user can change their sizes manually.

> * The "Enabled" checkbox changes text to "Disabled" without being checked. This is inconsistent and hard to understand.
> * I made it crash in some cases. I will try to recreate and describe this.

I will look at it. If you know how to reproduce it do not hesitate to tell me how.
These points should be addressed now.

I asked Claude Opus to do a code review for security, crash and UX issues.

Security Issues

1. No timeout on expression evaluation (DoS-self)
wslua_debugger.c:1317-1340 — wslua_debugger_evaluate() calls luaL_loadstring() + lua_pcall() with arbitrary user input. Entering while true do end will hang Wireshark permanently with no way to recover. While this is a self-inflicted DoS (not remotely exploitable), adding a lua_sethook-based instruction count limit would prevent freezes. The tooltip documents this limitation, but the impact (complete application hang requiring a force-kill) is too severe for a "just document it" approach.

2. Evaluated code can corrupt dissection state
wslua_debugger_evaluate() runs arbitrary Lua in the live dissector's Lua state. A user can accidentally do _G.some_proto = nil and corrupt ongoing analysis. Consider running evaluation in a sandboxed environment or at minimum warning more prominently before execution.

Potential Crash / Stability Issues

3. Nested event loop recursion via rapid stepping
lua_debugger_dialog.cpp:576-603 — onStep() calls wslua_debugger_step() which immediately fires the line hook, which calls handlePause(), which creates a new QEventLoop on the stack. Rapid stepping (holding F10) creates deeply nested stack frames of handlePause → loop.exec() → onStep → handlePause → loop.exec().... This can cause a stack overflow. Consider using a non-recursive approach (e.g., single persistent event loop with state flags).

4. Unprotected concurrent access to debugger.step_mode and temporary_breakpoint
wslua_debugger.c:391-410 — wslua_debugger_step() and wslua_debugger_continue() write to debugger.step_mode and debugger.temporary_breakpoint without holding the mutex, while wslua_debug_hook() reads them without the mutex. In the current design this is serialized by the nested event loop, but if the architecture ever changes (e.g., to async/non-blocking), these become data races. The mutex pattern is already used for breakpoints — step_mode and temporary_breakpoint should also be protected for consistency and safety.

5. Globals enumeration can freeze UI
wslua_debugger.c:975-1005 — wslua_debugger_get_variables("Globals") iterates _G without any limit. Wireshark's Lua state has hundreds (possibly thousands) of globals. Expanding "Globals" in the variables tree creates tree items for all of them, potentially freezing the UI. Consider adding a limit or lazy loading.

6. wslua_debugger_init called before lua_atpanic
In init_wslua.c, wslua_debugger_init(L) is called before lua_atpanic(L, wslua_panic). If the debugger init triggered any Lua error, it would use the default Lua panic handler (which calls abort()). In practice this is unlikely since wslua_debugger_init doesn't run Lua code, but the ordering is fragile.

UX Issues

7. Variables tree loses declaration order
lua_debugger_dialog.cpp:878-885 — After populating variables, the tree is sorted alphabetically (sortItems(0, Qt::AscendingOrder)). This loses the declaration order of local variables, which is typically more useful for debugging.

+/**

+ * This widget displays a clickable header that toggles the visibility

+class CollapsibleSection : public QWidget

+    Q_OBJECT
+
+  public:
+    /**
+     * @brief Construct a collapsible section.
+     * @param title The title displayed in the header.
+     * @param parent Optional parent widget.
+     */
+    explicit CollapsibleSection(const QString &title = QString(),
+                                QWidget *parent = nullptr);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Set the content widget for this section.
+     * @param contentWidget The widget to display when expanded.
+     *
+     * The section takes ownership of the widget.
+     */
+    void setContentWidget(QWidget *contentWidget);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Set the expanded state of the section.
+     * @param expanded True to expand, false to collapse.
+     */
+    void setExpanded(bool expanded);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Check if the section is currently expanded.
+     * @return True if expanded, false if collapsed.
+     */
+    bool isExpanded() const;
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Set the title text.
+     * @param title The new title.
+     */
+    void setTitle(const QString &title);

+     * @return The height of the header in pixels.
+     */
+    int headerHeight() const;

+    /**
+     * @brief Emitted when the section is toggled.
+     * @param expanded True if now expanded, false if collapsed.
+     */
+    void toggled(bool expanded);
+
+  private slots:
+    void onToggle(bool checked);
+
+  private:

+    QFrame *headerLine;
+    QWidget *contentArea;
+    QVBoxLayout *mainLayout;
+    int savedHeight;
+};

+#ifndef LUA_DEBUGGER_CODE_VIEW_H
+#define LUA_DEBUGGER_CODE_VIEW_H
+
+#include <QFont>
+#include <QObject>
+#include <QPlainTextEdit>
+#include <QtGlobal>
+
+class QSyntaxHighlighter;
+
+/**
+ * @brief Read-only code editor supporting gutter breakpoints and highlighting.
+ */
+class LuaDebuggerCodeView : public QPlainTextEdit
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+
+  public:
+    /**
+     * @brief Create the code view and configure the line number gutter.
+     * @param parent Optional parent widget for ownership.
+     */
+    LuaDebuggerCodeView(QWidget *parent = nullptr);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Paint the custom gutter that hosts line numbers and breakpoints.
+     * @param event Exposes the area to repaint.
+     */
+    void lineNumberAreaPaintEvent(QPaintEvent *event);
+    /**
+     * @brief Compute the width required for the gutter, including icons.
+     * @return Width in device-independent pixels.
+     */
+    qint32 lineNumberAreaWidth();
+
+    void setFilename(const QString &f) { filename = f; }
+    QString getFilename() const { return filename; }
+    /**
+     * @brief Highlight and scroll to the requested line.
+     * @param line Line number to select (1-based).
+     */
+    void setCurrentLine(qint32 line);
+    /** @brief Remove any current-line highlight from the view. */
+    void clearCurrentLineHighlight();
+    /** @brief Apply a monospace font to both editor text and gutter. */
+    void setEditorFont(const QFont &font);
+    /** @brief Refresh breakpoint markers in the gutter area. */
+    void updateBreakpointMarkers();
+    /** @brief Re-apply theme colors from the current preference. */
+    void applyTheme();
+
+  signals:
+    /** @brief Emitted when a breakpoint icon is clicked within the gutter. */
+    void breakpointToggled(const QString &filename, qint32 line);
+
+  protected:
+    /** @brief Update margins whenever Qt reports a size change. */
+    void resizeEvent(QResizeEvent *event) override;
+
+  private slots:
+    /** @brief Update margins to accommodate new block digits. */
+    void updateLineNumberAreaWidth(int newBlockCount);
+    /** @brief Recompute the highlight for the active line. */
+    void highlightCurrentLine();
+    /** @brief Repaint the gutter when Qt issues update requests. */
+    void updateLineNumberArea(const QRect &rect, int dy);
+
+  private:
+    QWidget *lineNumberArea;
+    qint32 currentLine;
+    QSyntaxHighlighter *syntaxHighlighter;
+
+    friend class LineNumberArea;
+    QString filename;
+    /** @brief Apply a VS Code inspired dark palette to the editor. */
+    void applyEditorPalette();
+};
+
+class LineNumberArea : public QWidget
+{
+  public:
+    /**
+     * @brief Construct the helper widget bound to a specific code view.
+     * @param editor Owning code editor responsible for painting content.
+     */
+    LineNumberArea(LuaDebuggerCodeView *editor)
+        : QWidget(editor), codeEditor(editor)
+    {
+    }
+
+    /** @brief Size the gutter according to the editor's width requirements. */
+    QSize sizeHint() const override
+    {
+        return QSize(codeEditor->lineNumberAreaWidth(), 0);
+    }
+
+  protected:
+    /** @brief Delegate painting back to the code view. */
+    void paintEvent(QPaintEvent *event) override
+    {
+        codeEditor->lineNumberAreaPaintEvent(event);
+    }
+
+    /** @brief Toggle breakpoints when the gutter is clicked. */
+    void mousePressEvent(QMouseEvent *event) override;
+
+  private:
+    LuaDebuggerCodeView *codeEditor;
+};
+
+#endif // LUA_DEBUGGER_CODE_VIEW_H
